claims.text: Tungsten particles will be pre-coated with a thin vapor-deposited Ni layer before spark plasma sintering.
The Ni interlayer will enhance interfacial bonding between tungsten and copper.
The Ni interlayer will reduce interfacial void formation in W–Cu composites.
The Ni interlayer will reduce phase separation in W–Cu composites.
The Ni-coated composite will preserve mechanical durability and thermal transport under fusion-reactor irradiation conditions.
Conventionally powder-metallurgy-processed W–Cu materials typically exhibit inhomogeneous dispersion.
Conventionally powder-metallurgy-processed W–Cu materials typically contain interfacial voids and phase separation.
Inhomogeneity, interfacial voids, and phase separation impair thermal transport in W–Cu materials.
Applying the Ni coating at low temperature will avoid alteration of the tungsten structure.
A vapor-deposited Ni coating will produce a conformal, thin interlayer between tungsten and copper.
The Ni interlayer acts as a graded interface between tungsten and copper.
The Ni interlayer lowers the interfacial-energy mismatch between tungsten and copper.
Lowering the interfacial-energy mismatch promotes wetting during sintering.
The Ni interlayer promotes interdiffusion during sintering.
Improved W–Cu interfacial contact minimizes void formation and phase separation.
A more uniform W–Cu microstructure supports enhanced thermal conductivity.
A more uniform W–Cu microstructure supports mechanical durability under irradiation.

Relative to uncoated W–Cu composites, Ni-coated samples will have statistically significantly lower interfacial void content, greater microstructural homogeneity, improved thermal conductivity, and maintained or enhanced mechanical performance.
Direct SPS and mechanical alloying without tungsten pre-coating are existing fabrication baselines.
SPS-based powder metallurgy is applicable to W-containing materials intended for high-temperature or fusion plasma-facing service.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome permits mechanical performance to be merely maintained, whereas the falsification rule requires improved mechanical performance; a result allowed by the prediction could therefore be classified as falsifying.
